message:
Update L. 116 of backbone.py

When fine-tuning the network for our own problem, we encountered the error RuntimeError: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been modified by an inplace operation: [torch.cuda.FloatTensor [32, 768, 248]].

This seemed to be triggered by the in place operation occuring L. 116.  To solve this we replaced `x += x_conv` by `x = x.clone() + x_conv`

author: Ilya Pasechnikov <ilya.pasechnikov@arcadia.spb.ru>
message:
Add memory safe constructors to TensorConfig and MatrixConfig

These new constructors work with std::shared_ptr and std::vector

 - std::vector constructors copy all the passed data. They are the safest one.
   You can't go wrong with them.

 - std::shared_ptr constructors don't copy data. They are kind of dangerous but the most perfomant ones.
   For sure it's much safer than raw pointers, cause it's hard to leak shared pointers.
   But still you have to be careful and know what you are doing because this data can be
   shared between different structures.
   But in some cases it can be really handy, if you want to remove an old matrix but
   create a new one with the same data and you are sure that no other data structure shares this same data.
   Or it's really intentional and you want to share data.

author: Jakub Kaczmarzyk <jakub.kaczmarzyk@gmail.com>
message:
install local autokeras + update tensorflow and keras-tuner version

This commit halves the size of the autokeras Docker image. TensorFlow is updated to 2.3.0, and keras-tuner is updated to 1.0.2rc1. In addition, the local copy of autokeras is used. This is helpful if changes are made to autokeras and a developer would like to test the changes in a Docker image, building the Docker image will use the local copy of the code. Last, the cache is not used in `pip install` to reduce the size of the built image.

author: Jakub Kaczmarzyk <jakub.kaczmarzyk@gmail.com>
message:
install local autokeras + update tensorflow and keras-tuner version

This commit halves the size of the autokeras Docker image. TensorFlow is updated to 2.3.0, and keras-tuner is updated to 1.0.2rc1. In addition, the local copy of autokeras is used. This is helpful if changes are made to autokeras and a developer would like to test the changes in a Docker image, building the Docker image will use the local copy of the code. Last, the cache is not used in `pip install` to reduce the size of the built image.

message: Baseline, working first stab at 1D classifier for autokeras re-using much of the existing autokeras functionality. Included is an example, pytest files, and documentation in comments, with low-hanging fruit suggestions for further improvements. It does not work as well as I'd like (auto-generated topologies are not optimal for 1D problems, and typically do far better with manual topologies, but I'm a data scientist....) However, it is a working first-stab at autokeras functionality for auto-generating 1D numerical classifiers. (It's suggested that further extending this code by auto-subsituting numeric labels for text strings would then result in a first-stab generalized classifier.) Some further tweaks to the Bayesian topology generated to optimize it for 1D rather than 2D problems should greatly improve this code.

author: Martin Klosi <mklosi@23andme.com>
message:
Allow custom hyper_parameters object in fit method

addresses, but does not resolve #1373

Using these changes, along with providing "seed" to the AutoModel constructor, one can retrain a model on the best hyper parameters found from a previous run. Also one can constrain the search space only to certain values, including number of units in each layer.

Example usage:

```
input_node = ak.StructuredDataInput()
output_node = ak.StructuredDataBlock()(input_node)
output_node = ak.RegressionHead()(output_node)

auto_model = ak.AutoModel(
    inputs=input_node,
    outputs=output_node,
    seed=self.seed,
)

hp = HyperParameters()
hp.Fixed("structured_data_block_1/normalize", True)
hp.Fixed("structured_data_block_1/dense_block_1/num_layers", 2)
hp.Fixed("structured_data_block_1/dense_block_1/use_batchnorm", True)
hp.Fixed("structured_data_block_1/dense_block_1/dropout", 0.5)
hp.Fixed("structured_data_block_1/dense_block_1/units_0", 32)
hp.Choice("structured_data_block_1/dense_block_1/units_1", [32, 64, 128, 256])
hp.Fixed("regression_head_1/dropout", 0.25)

auto_model.fit(
    x=df_train_X,
    y=df_train_y,
    hp=hp
)
```

Corrected NHANES data and Juptyer notebook

Whereas poverty index previously could be up to 999, poverty index now is maximum of 9.98, in line with the NHANES definition of poverty index. Poverty index that was previously '999' is now 'Nan', since 999 is a code for 'unknown'. Whereas "Red blood cells" previously was maximum 88.8, red blood cells (in millions/mm^3) was scaled down by a factor of ten, to correspond correctly to the NHANES DU4800 documentation. 'Unacceptable data' and 'Blank, but applicable' (previously 77.7 and 88.8) are now 'NaN'.

author: Scott Lundberg <slund1@cs.washington.edu>
message:
New interface for v0.20

This is a big interface change where we no longer return the expected model output as the last column of the shap_values array. This makes KernelExplainer and TreeExplainer consistent with DeepExplainer, and also now requires us to pass `explainer.expected_value` to `force_plot` calls (since the base value is no longer the last column).

This should make everything much clearer in the long run, since now the shape of the returned shap_values matrix is the exact same as the passed input matrix.

* introduce max_val parameter in image plot

To keep scale of color-coding consistent during multiple explanations on the same image.

For example, I have been working on an app where you compute explanation for the same image at different times during training, to see how feature importance changes during training (in a particular setting where this make sense: Continual Learning. I am visualizing catastrophic forgetting)
But if scale of the color-coding changes at every plot, the sequence of explanation doen't make sense anymore (visually)

message:
FIX: plots.image show labels for every row if provided (#4113)

* plots.image show labels for all rows if provided

Fixes https://github.com/shap/shap/issues/4112

First fix the labels reshape in case the labels are provided as a list.
Currently this creates an array of shape (1, nb_of_provided_labels).

If a list of list of labels is provided (# samples, # top_k classes),
this results in shape (1, # samples x # top_k classes), which does not
work when adding the labels to the plot later on.

This commit changes the reshaping logic to have labels with shape
(# samples, # top_k classes).
In case only one set of labels are provided in the list, the resulting
shape will be (1, # top_k classes).

Then we fix the actual plotting, where now only labels are added for the
first row, even if labels per row are provided (e.g. when using the
labels straight from the explainer, or when providing a 2D array, or a
list of lists). Thanks to the reshaping fix all these cases work.

Users can now decide to use the Explainer's labels, or provided them
manually with this flexibility:
- Separate labels for each sample (in the form of a 2D array, a list of
lists, or a flat list)
- One set of labels to be used for all samples (in the form of a flat
list, a 1D array, a 2D array (with first dim 1), a list containting 1
list).

Only requirement is that the number of labels provided is either:
- # samples x # top_k classes
- 1 x # top_k classes

Cases that have been tested, using the example mentioned in #4112 (in
turn a very slightly adapted version of the ResNet 50 tutorial):

Producing labels for every row:
```
shap.image_plot(shap_values)
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=[['a','b','c'],
                                     ['d','e','f']])
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=np.array([['a','b','c'],
                                              ['d','e','f']]))
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=['a','b','c','d','e','f'])
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=np.array(['a','b','c','d','e','f']))
```

Producing labels only for the first row:
(This was the intention of https://github.com/shap/shap/pull/3636)
```
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=['a', 'b', 'c'])
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=np.array(['a','b','c']))
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=[['a', 'b', 'c']])
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=np.array([['a','b','c']]))
```

* test plots.image when labels are (not) provided

Test `image_plot()` for use cases where:
- User does not provide labels (use the ones from the Explanation)
- User provides labels for each image
- User only provides one set of labels for all images

* type annotation for case of list of list of labels

Support the use case where labels for each image are provided as a list
of list of str.

* changes and type annotations to pass mypy

* Refactor creation of explanation into a fixture

To be able to reuse the created explanation object in other tests.

Also corrected the `output_names` in the explanation object which should
have as many elements as there are classes, not images.

* tests compare against baseline image with labels

Change the tests so they can compare against baseline images instead of
merely checking they do not produce an error.

Reused the existing logic from `test_image_multi` thanks to refactoring
the creation of the explanation object into a fixture in the previous
commit.

This introduces 3 new image comparisons:
- No labels are provided (the ones from the explanation
are then used by default, first row only)
- Different labels per row are provided as a list of lists
- Different labels per row are provided as a np.array

The existing test case already covered:
- One set of labels is provided as a list

message:
refactor: Cohorts internals, use @property, add type hinting and expose it in docs (#3779)

* refactor: use property to enforce types in cohorts

* fix: remove __call__ since Explanation has no call

NOTE: this is because we had enforced `cohorts[k]` to always be an
Explanation upon property setting.
And Explanation has no `__call__` attribute (error thrown by mypy), so
it makes no sense for cohorts to have it as well.

* docs: Expose Cohorts as public API in the docs

* apply review suggestions

* fix: populate cohorts dict rather than modify one by one

This prevents the subtle bug where we can accidentally add in a non-Explanation object

* chore: add tests for Cohorts

* fix: add __call__ back

for invoking methods after they have been getattr-ed, e.g. cohort.mean(axis=0)

* fix: mypy complaints

* include review suggestion

less intrusive, and the improvements should compound with each other.

author: Bhanuday Sharma <55601693+bhanudaysharma@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Update _monitoring.py

If the 'inc' is greater than or equal to len(ys)-inc, the subsequent for loop does not run. Hence, the list pvals remains empty. As a result, np.min(pvals) fails resulting in failure of the entire monitoring_plot function. So, I corrected this error by allowing the user to choose 'inc' value at runtime by passing it as an argument to the function. Set the default value as 50 for backward compatibility. If (inc < len(ys)-inc), the t-test is skipped and a Warning is produced to prevent the failure of function of monitoring_plot.

message:
Fixes error with XGBoost 1.1

In the new XGBoost (1.1), `.save_raw()` output is slightly different, which means that `TreeExplainer` doesn't work. See issue #1215. 
The build is currently failing for this reason, with all XGBoost tests failing.

The fix here is to just remove the prefix 'binf' from the model buffer, which as been added in the new version (either intentionally or accidentally - I can't find a PR in XGBoost which mentions this change.)

Fixes #1215

stored as an array of numpy.float64):
```python

    128             yticklabels[rng[i]] = format_value(float(features[order[i]]), "%0.03f") + " = " + feature_names[order[i]]
    129         else:
--> 130             yticklabels[rng[i]] = features[order[i]] + " = " + feature_names[order[i]]
    132 # add a last grouped feature to represent the impact of all the features we didn't show
    133 if num_features < len(values):

UFuncTypeError: ufunc 'add' did not contain a loop with signature matching types (dtype('bool'), dtype('<U3')) -> None
```

It still works with native python type, ie.
```python
a=5.0
np.issubdtype(type(a), np.number)
True
```

An alternative solution is to switch the if/else and test for string
first.

message:
Added feature to alter the texts on plots, i.e. for multi-language

Extracted the text values from the plot functions into global constants. The official name is Monkey Patching (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monkey_patch). It is a simple pattern to enable to change the texts of the plots without changing the functions.

Example code:

import shap

shap.plots.SHAP_MAIN_EFFECT = "Translation for SHAP main effect value for\n%s"
shap.plots.SHAP_INTERACTION_VALUE = "Translation for SHAP interaction value"
shap.plots.SHAP_INTERACTION_EFFECT = "Translation for SHAP interaction value for\n%s and %s"
shap.plots.SHAP_VALUE = "Translation for SHAP value (impact on model output)"
shap.plots.SHAP_VALUE_FOR = "Translation for SHAP value for\n%s"
shap.plots.SHAP_PLOT_FOR = "Translation for SHAP plot for %s"
shap.plots.SHAP_FEATURE = "Translation for Feature %s"
shap.plots.SHAP_FEATURE_VALUE = "Translation for Feature value"
shap.plots.SHAP_FEATURE_VALUE_LOW = "Translation for Low"
shap.plots.SHAP_FEATURE_VALUE_HIGH = "Translation for High"
shap.plots.SHAP_JOINT_VALUE = "Translation for Joint SHAP value"

author: Jules van Rie <jules@vanrie.be>
message:
plots.image show labels for all rows if provided

Fixes https://github.com/shap/shap/issues/4112

First fix the labels reshape in case the labels are provided as a list.
Currently this creates an array of shape (1, nb_of_provided_labels).

If a list of list of labels is provided (# samples, # top_k classes),
this results in shape (1, # samples x # top_k classes), which does not
work when adding the labels to the plot later on.

This commit changes the reshaping logic to have labels with shape
(# samples, # top_k classes).
In case only one set of labels are provided in the list, the resulting
shape will be (1, # top_k classes).

Then we fix the actual plotting, where now only labels are added for the
first row, even if labels per row are provided (e.g. when using the
labels straight from the explainer, or when providing a 2D array, or a
list of lists). Thanks to the reshaping fix all these cases work.

Users can now decide to use the Explainer's labels, or provided them
manually with this flexibility:
- Separate labels for each sample (in the form of a 2D array, a list of
lists, or a flat list)
- One set of labels to be used for all samples (in the form of a flat
list, a 1D array, a 2D array (with first dim 1), a list containting 1
list).

Only requirement is that the number of labels provided is either:
- # samples x # top_k classes
- 1 x # top_k classes

Cases that have been tested, using the example mentioned in #4112 (in
turn a very slightly adapted version of the ResNet 50 tutorial):

Producing labels for every row:
```
shap.image_plot(shap_values)
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=[['a','b','c'],
                                     ['d','e','f']])
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=np.array([['a','b','c'],
                                              ['d','e','f']]))
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=['a','b','c','d','e','f'])
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=np.array(['a','b','c','d','e','f']))
```

Producing labels only for the first row:
(This was the intention of https://github.com/shap/shap/pull/3636)
```
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=['a', 'b', 'c'])
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=np.array(['a','b','c']))
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=[['a', 'b', 'c']])
shap.image_plot(shap_values, labels=np.array([['a','b','c']]))
```

message:
Critical Fix: backward permutation of PermutationExplainer unused

PermutationExplainer evaluates the model on both the forward and backward permutations but the output of the backward permutation is never used yielding an evaluation of the model of (up to) twice the amount of data needed and a potentially drastic slowdown of the model agnostic explainer. This fix includes the backward permutation in the SHAP value estimates.

message:
ENH: minor speedups in non-tree KernelExplainer (#3983)

* ENH: minor speedups in non-tree KernelExplainer

* A few minor simplifications/adjustments that seem to give about 5-10%
better performance for non-tree `KernelExplainer` for the scenario
described at gh-3943.

* I don't think we have formal `asv`-style benchmarks in this project,
but informal testing with 5 trials each (times in seconds)
for the reproducer in the above issue (on an ARM Mac):
- `master`:     52.803, 50.711, 51.503, 50.613, 51.348
- this branch:  47.557, 47.128, 48.197, 47.651, 47.216

* This is less impactful than then improvements at gh-3944, but also
less intrusive, and the improvements should compound with each other.

Co-authored-by: Aaron R Hall <arhall@lanl.gov>

* MAINT: PR 3983 revisions

* Expand the handling of array/object types in `not_equal()`
based on reviewer feedback. Add a related test that fails
when using the naive `i == j` fallback.

for more information, see https://pre-commit.ci

* MAINT, TST: PR 3983 revisions

* Relax the stringency of the numeric closeness check
in `test_explainer_non_number_dtype`, which was failing in CI.

author: Tyler Reddy <tyler.je.reddy@gmail.com>
message:
ENH: support rng for summary_plot

* Some folks on my team are having issues writing tests
downstream of `shap` because `summary_plot` mutates
the NumPy legacy random machinery global state, which is
hard to work around in a large testsuite. It would be
great if a heavily-used project in the ML space like `shap`
could start to adopt support for local random `Generator`
objects per the community document at:
https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0007/
This PR is a lot cruder than that approach, but appears
to allow preservation of the current global state behavior
while allowing the option of using the modern non-global
approach for downstream developers that need it.

* This patch adds a regression test that fails when not
using the optional `rng` argument, and passes when
it is used to scope to a local random state. If there
is a preference for using the full SPEC 7 approach
(and that may very well be the best idea), I may ask
one of my team members to help out a bit, since they
will benefit from it.

* The full testsuite passed locally via `pytest --import-mode=append`

author: Martin Losch <30285667+mjlosch@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
penetrating shortwave fraction as a 3D-field (#750)

* introduce global field SWFrac3D that is computed once

- to be used as a lookup table during the timestep
- may be used to included BGC-contributions to light attenuation
- so far, KPP is not included in this

* cleanup: remove SWFracB entirely from pkg/seaice

* add flag KPP_USE_SWFRAC3D to use precomputed SWFrac3D

instead of computed SWFRAC locally. This changes results. Use AD of
1D_ocean_ice_column as a test for the new flag

* replace local swfrac computation by precomputed SWFrac3D field

and test this code in cfc_example by defining SHORTWAVE_HEATING (not
used, i.e. does not change results)

* revert model/inc/CPP_OPTIONS.h to original state, add local version

to cfc_example to test pkg/layers/SHORTWAVE_HEATIING related
changes (fix previous error)

* fix a small bug for Nr=1 with pkg/seaice

* increase k-size of SWFrac3D to Nr+1 and adjust logic

to retain the symmetry between z- and p-coordinates. Simplifies code
in many places

* introduce runtime parameter selectPenetratingSW

0: do not allow penetration below surface layer
1: allow constant-in-time penetration below surface layer
2: allow time dependent penetration below surface layer according to
local attenuation (not implemented)
default = 0 if SHORTWAVE_HEATING undefined and 1 if defined

* use new parameter selectPenetratingSW in pkg/seaice and pkg/kpp

* adjust field and parameter descriptions and definition

* revert because it still works without the change

and because this file is deprecated and should not be developed any
further

* change IF selectPenetratingSW from .GE. 0 to .GT. 0

to make selectPenetratingSW==0 equivalent to
undef SHORTWAVE_HEATING (as intended)

* adjust condition to selectPenetrating .GT. 0

* revert file because change causes differences due to truncation

* always load Qsw from file, if file exists

* revert back all changes

* bring back selectPenetratingSW

to be consistent with APPLY_FORCING_T, only remove Qsw if selectPenetratingSW > 0

* use same method as in external_forcing_surf.F to in-/exclude Qsw

* minor: skip loops if not needed

* unsensitive to z or p origin

Take care of case where seaLev_Z <> 0 (in z-coord.) or top_Pres <> 0 (in p-coord)
since, for consistency, SWFrac3D needs to be exactly 1 at the top.

* revert line breaks in comments

* change "KPPfrac" definition

to be the fraction of Short-Wave flux heating the mixing layer, i.e.,
 "new KPPfrac" = 1 minus "old KPPfrac"

* change to also work with "#undef SHORTWAVE_HEATING"

* replace new KPP_USE_SWFRAC3D flag by runtime flag

* linear interpolation of SWFrac3D/swatt between interfaces

* adjust store directives

* clean up kpp_calc.F before it becomes more complicated again

- replace work-arrays where possible, because their re-use confuse TAF
- rename work array work2 into sdens (surface density)
- new work array workf to compute swfrac; the double use of worka
  confuses TAF
- adjust comments
- adjust store directives to avoid recomputation of most of kpp_calc
- fix a store directive bug (store KPPhbl(:,:,bi,bj) instead of KPPhbl)

* adjust store directives and add some comments

many store directives can be avoided by incomplete statements for
worka; the re-use of worka and the fact that it is used input/output
of swfrac causes a lot of headache

* improve new param description

also remove one commented line (left from previous version)

* remove old commented out lines

   day[time,iter,date] -> obs[time,iter,date], yday -> yobs,
   dayspermon -> daysperavgperiod

* change leftover local variable etaday to etagcm

* Add comment and additional checks for use_mon, clean up comments

* fix line continuation bug

* change check of 'mon' and 'MON' to 'month' and 'MONTH'

* Add check that tp/ers/gfo must have the same avgperiod, improve check for use_mon

* fix bug: remove extra endif

* fix mis-spell and minor errors

* little simplification (+ safer)

- gencost_avgperiod is a 5 character string so no need to specify (1:5)
  when comparing to 'MONTH' or 'month' (similar to  ecco_readparms.F & ecco_cost_init_fixed.F)
- make sure the check in "ecco_check.F" matches the setting of "use_mon" in cost_gencost_sshv4.F
  (where we don't test if gencost_avgperiod is 'day  ' when it's not 'month').

* simplify: remove unused local vars

 'GM_K3D_T' --> 'GM_BaK_T'
on/off switch:
 GM_useK3D  --> GM_useBatesK3d
3-D array:
 K3D        -->  GM_BatesK3d
Parameters:
 GM_K3D_*   --> GM_Bates_*

streamice_cg_solve_petsc, add parameter to control fill level

and consistently update verification/halfpipe_streamice/code* copies

message:
documentation for this:
introduce "adaptive EVP" by Madlen Kimmritz
  - this is an intermediate state of a truely converging EVP that has
    the potential of outperforming implicit VP methods, I do not recommend
    using it yet.
  - for now, "adaptive EVP" is turned on by setting SEAICE_EVP_USE_ADAPTATION
    and all parameters are hardwired
  - for convergence it still requires very smooth regularisations, that means,
    if SEAICE_DELTA_SMOOTHREG is defined, deltaCreg=deltaC+deltaMin, which is
    different from the VP case with deltaCreg=sqrt(deltaC**2+deltaMin**2); also
    specific averaging appears to be required, still subject to tuning
  - still needs cleaning and I need to turn parameter into runtime parameters
  - add code to compute and print residuals of iteration, compile with
    defining ALLOW_SEAICE_EVP_RESIDUAL to enable it

author: Jean-Michel Campin <jmc@ocean.mit.edu>
message:
Disable "Check for Fortran Compiler" part

It turns out that the running test part does not ever terminate when tried on
compute node; the reason beeing related to (hard to use) mpiexec:

From Archer Helpdesk Team:
 When running on a login node, there is no mpiexec. When running on a PP node,
 there is, in /opt/pbs/12.2.401.141761/bin/mpiexec. This runs a user-supplied mpiexec,
 and tries to not run itself (in an infinite recursion) but fails because it compares
 the strings /opt/pbs/default/bin (where PBS thinks the bin directory is) and
 /opt/pbs/12.2.401.141761/bin (the directory in PATH). This is an error in the PBS
 script (or in Archer's configuration).

By setting: FC_CHECK=f in optfile, the whole "Check for Fortran Compiler"
is skipped.

We now officially use the predictor-corrector terminology.
We make the prediction step at the end of the dynamics() section
and store the result in the gUNm1, gVNm1, gTNm1 arrays.
The "tricky" part is that at the beginning of the dynamics section,
where the "correction" is made, theses arrays must be initialised
at the beginning of any run. A new routine init_predictor() does this.
This is "all" in preparation for implicit diffusion. Let's hope
it's enough...

author: Alistair Adcroft <aadcroft@princeton.edu>
message:
o Created mechanism for make makefile to use $TOOLSDIR variable of Makefile
   - previously it recorded the actual invocation of genmake2 which meant
     that editing TOOLSDIR was not sufficient to be able to move the set-up
 o In addition to everything else, we now record the pkg configuration in
   the Makefile
   - previously the configuration was only recorded in PACKAGES_CONFIG.h
     and gm_state
 o Created targets for Makefile:
   PACKAGES_CONFIG.h:  this allows "make" to create the pkg config file
                       given the configuration state that is now recorded
                       in Makefile
   AD_CONFIG.h:        creates the appropriate null adj config file for
                       compiling the forward model
 o The switching of AD_CONFIG.h is unchanged but the files used for comparison
   of the state are now created only briefly by make and only for the duration
   of the comparison
   - previously these files were left in place and an inadvertent deletion
    required a new invocation of genmake2
 o Added new "generic" script for converting cmd-line cpp options to cpp
   statements in a file
 o Created a file in tools/adjoint_sed containing the sed commands needed
   to patch back myThid in adjoint code. This file used to be created in
   the CWD by genmake2

Comments:
 o genmake2, make   now works without the make depend phase
   - this is necessary (and was an old feature) for occasions when makedepend
     is not available and xmakedepend doesn't work or is too slow to be useful
 o make clean   now deletes all temporary files (except FC_NAMEMANGLE.h) so
   that make CLEAN only leaves the Makefile and the Makefile now contains
   sufficient information to rebuild everything. This was a capability of
   the old genmake.

author: Ou Wang <34174618+owang01@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Add extra diagnostic variables (#560)

* Add extra diagnostic variables

* Add diagnostics for steric height

* Calculate mass integral using finite-volume form

* Two more updates

1) Define and output new diagnostics inside pkg/ecco
2) Update how steric height (sterht) is calculated

* fix so that it compiles:

a) move icalculation of RHOInSituLoc outside #ifdef ALLOW_PSBAR_STERIC
  since it's used in "m_bp" calculation.
b) protect calls to diagnostics pkg within #ifdef ALLOW_DIAGNOSTICS
   (and "IF ( useDiagnostics ) THEN") so that it compiles without it

* add few missing declarations (so that it compiles).

* Add argument myTime and myIter to S/R ECCO_PHYS

This allows to differentiate between early call from ecco_init_varia.F
(called from packages_init_variables.F) and regular call from forward_step.F
and to fill diagnostics only in second case.

* New S/R ECCO_INIT_FIXED

This new S/R (called in place of ecco_cost_init_fixed) is just calling
ECCO_COST_INIT_FIXED  and new S/R ECCO_DIAGNOSTICS_INIT.
This allows to move all diagnostics initialisation out of ecco_cost_init_fixed.F
(which is no longer affected by this PR).

* skip recomputing density by using "rhoInSitu" (from common block)

- this is make mass and bottom pressure more consistent (since later one was
  computed by vertical integral of the same density field).
- this also save the cost of recomputing the density (not negligeable, e.g. if using TEOS-10).
- keep the call to FIND_RHO_2D when called from ecco_init_varia.F (rhoInSitu is zero
  at this stage).

* Move few 2-D vars out of ECCO.h common blocks

The few 2-D variables in ECCO.h that are only used in ecco_phys.F and nowhere else
are now declared locally in this S/R (and moved out of common block). This simplifies
the code by reducing potential dependencies.

Also remove few unused vars in ecco_phys.F and move one k-loop outside i,j loops.

* initialise m_UE & m_VN over full size

also fix 1 typo in comments + minor edits (spacing)

* document adding extra diagnostics in pkg/ecco

author: Martin Losch <30285667+mjlosch@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
advection in AD-Mode (#404)

* remove unnecessary inAdMode if statement

This is a bit of a clean up

* add new parameter useApproxAdvectionInAdMode to replace inAdMode

- inAdMode is used unspecifically in more than one context so it's
  difficult to find out what it really does, so we replace it for
  advection by a specific parameter
- if useApproxAdvectionInAdMode is True and advection scheme 33 use
  advection scheme 30 in AD-model in seaice_advection, gad_advection
  and gad_calc_rsh, model stops when parameters are set inconsistently
- defaults to False, but is reset to True if inAdExact = False to be
  backwards compatible

* fix logic for new flag and add comments

- use inAdMode always with either inAdExact or
  useApproximateAdvectionInAdMode
- set inAdTrue/False also when useApproximateAdvectionInAdMode = True
- this is a larger change than anticipated and requires a careful review

* use advection scheme 33 and useApproxAdvectionInAdMode in this test

* Update refence output for AD & TLM seaice test

Needed since T & S advection-scheme and seaice advection-scheme have been changed
from 30 to 33, (+ useApproxAdvectionInAdMode).

* improve warning message

* attempt of implementing a consistent spacing policy

* set inAdMode to hard coded values in autodiff_inadmode_set/unset_ad

- this changes the meaning of parameter inAdMode something that the
  name implies (in my view), but it also requires that inAdMode needs
  to be used together with, e.g., adInExact or any other similar
  flags. Currently the only other implemented flag is
  useApproxAdvectionInAdMode
- remove parameters inAdTrue/False and

* refine check for advection schemes with useApproxAdvectionInAdMode

* remove SOLVE_MAX_TMP and simplify code in seaice_lsr

- add a check in seaice_check so make sure that
  SEAICElinearIterMax <= SOLV_MAX_FIXED
- doesn't change results but requires to set SEAICElinearIterMax =
  500 (default for SOLV_MAX_FIXED) in some AD experiments

* simplify the implementation of useApproxAdvectionInAdMode

as per suggestion of Jean-Michel Campin, the related code is now
only a couple of lines in one place per subroutine which makes it also
much easier to extend the scheme to other advection schemes.

* small fix: replace vertAvecScheme by vertAdvecSchArg in if-statement

* Avoid setting default that prevent the model to run

- when pkg/autodiff is compiled, change default value of seaice parameter "SEAICElinearIterMax"
  so that it does not cause an error (and stop) in seaice_check.F
- revert update of parameter file "data.seaice" in few AD experiment (no need
  to explicitly set this parameter there).

* Change a WARNING to a STOP

In the case where pkg/generic_advdiff is not compiled but useApproxAdvectionInAdMode=T,
change the Warning to a Stop (since any of the relevant code is not even compiled).

* Document advection in AD-Mode changes

author: Alistair Adcroft <aadcroft@princeton.edu>
message:
Modified the "lopping" procedure for determining the fraction cell
height.

The original formulation first filter the model depth using
the hFacMin parameter. Any fractional cells less than hFacMin
were rounded to the nearer of 0 or hFacMin. Then the depths were
filtered using hFacMinDr where the actual size was tested.
This meant that some cells could be rounded twice and also
that if hFacMinDr was specified as larger than the nominal
thickness that the fractional cell thickness could end up
larger than 1. Clearly a bad idea (?) but to cause this one
would have to specify the hFacMin and hFacMinDr parameters in
a inconsistent way.

The new method combines hFacMin and hFacMinDr first and then
does a single filtering of model depths. If hFacMinDr is
greater than the nominal layer thickness, the later is used
and the fractional cell thicknesses are set to 1. Otherwise,
layers thicknesses are rounded to using the larger of
hFacMin and hFacMinDr/drF(K).

Using the new method, setting hFacMin=0 and hFacMin=100
means that lopping only occurs for cell thicker than 100
and the minimum cell thickness of lopped cells will be 100.
This, I think, is a much cleaner specification. AJA.

author: Ian G Fenty <Ian.Fenty@jpl.nasa.gov>
message:
Minor changes to seaice package.

1) Retired old variables (A22, SEAICE_lhsublim, areaMax, areaMin, hiceMin) and
   added some new ones (SEAICE_area_reg, SEAICE_hice_reg, SEAICE_area_floor)

  - Differentiated "regularization variables" from "floor variables"
    * areaMin became SEAICE_area_reg (old A22) and SEAICE_area_floor
    * hiceMin became SEAICE_hice_reg (old hiceMin)
     (with _reg meaning regularization variable)

  - SEAICE_lhSublim becomes lhSublim, the sum of SEAICE_lhEvap and SEAICE_lhFusion
    so as to ensure energy conservation when going between phases

  - A22 was not used anywhere

2) Changed regularization procedure for heffActual and hsnowActual to ensure
   well-boundedness and smooth adjoint in seaice_growth.F

3) Fixed a bug where seaice_solve4temp would not recognize ice-free grid cells
   because the old regularization always set heffActual >= 0.05 cm

4) Changed the model so that the default behavior is to put a small (10^-5) "floor"
   on AREA when HEFF > 0.
   - went from requiring ALLOW_PRECLUDE_INFINITESIMAL_AREA to be defined to
     requiring that DISABLE_AREA_FLOOR *not* be defined

 Modified Files:
 	SEAICE_PARAMS.h seaice_check.F seaice_growth.F
 	seaice_readparms.F seaice_solve4temp.F seaice_summary.F

scaling by Nx*Ny makes little sense

experiment global_ocean.cs32x15.icedyn, and revert

author: Martin Losch <30285667+mjlosch@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
adjust taf directives in gad_som_advect and seaice_solve4temp (#594)

* reduce size of local tape, because it is not even a common block

* get rid of 16 recomputation warnings and associated recomputations

by storing on local tapes

* some tweaks and corrections (of print statements)

* avoid another 14 recomp warnings and associated recomputations

by defining small local tapes

* change 2 ALLOW_AUTODIFF to ALLOW_AUTODIFF_TAMC

also bring back 1 line of comment that got removed

* suppress two recomputation warnings at no extra cost

but leave two more untouched because they lead to more memory
requirements without any gain.

* replace maxpass by maxcube; set maxcube=2 in tracers_adjsens/tamc.h

* add more error output (to be improved)

* remove duplicate "check & stop" for npass > maxcube

also change to more standard error message report (to STDERR)

* changed my mind: do it right and avoid local recomputations

* Fix storage dir size in Multi-Dim advection S/R

- consistently use "maxcube" (instead of "maxpass") for maximum number of horizontal
  direction in Multi-Dim advection subroutine and pkg/seaice advection subroutine ;
  depending on the value of these 2 parameters, this fix is saving memory space (e.g.,
  when using many pTracers) or avoid potential problem (no ptracers, maxpass=2, but
  using cubeSphereExchange).
- adjust storage dir initialisation and storage key calculation; improve/adjust comments
  in reference "tamc.h" and change default maxcube to 2.
- update few verification experiments "tamc.h" version (changing maxcube from 1 to 2).

* minor: remove consecutive blank lines

* Change "maxcube" from 3 to 2

to use multi-dimensional advection on "maxcube" needs to be set to 2 or 3 for cube-sphere
like grid. Since this is not the case in these set-up, can safely change it to 2.

* document improving/fixing advection and seaice local tapes

  hFacMin   - is the lower limit for water fraction in a cell
  hFacMinDz - is the lower limit for water thickness in lopped cells

  To force full cells, using continuous bathymetry, set hFacMin=1

1) to make it easier to compare with P-coords similar set-up, set gravity to 10. (instead of 9.81)

   reduce viscosity and use simple harmonic horizontal viscosity (instead of biharmonic),

   selectCoriScheme=1 (i.e., Jamar & Ozer, 1995), set vertical interface at the middle between
   two level center (set delRc instead of delR).

   still stable with 1.h time-step (= twice current time-step).

author: Jean-Michel Campin <jmc@ocean.mit.edu>
message:
Turn off CPP option: ALLOW_AUTODIFF_INIT_OLD

This CPP option was added by @gaelforget in Dec 2015 to enable to reproduce old results.
Although it was not well documented as "fixing a bug" when left #undef (and, when #define,
"adding an old bug", from mid 2004), it is certainly the case.
The corresponding (wrong) code in autodiff_init_varia.F which is added back when CPP
option ALLOW_AUTODIFF_INIT_OLD is defined, does 2 wrong things:
1) it resets 2-D fields "dEtaHdt" after loading this field from pickup-files. This breaks
  the restart and affects all four AD global_ocean_cs32x15 experiments (all starting from
  pickup files that do contains non-zero "dEtaHdt" field).
2) it reset 2-D field "EmPmR" when pkg/exf is compiled. This will not cause any problem
  (and has no effect in any of the four AD global_ocean_cs32x15 experiments) if pkg/exf
  is used or if periodicExternalForcing=.TRUE., (in these 2 cases EmPmR is then loaded later);
  However, in case a constant in time EmPmRFile is used (periodicExternalForcing=F)
  and pkg/exf is compiled but not used (useEXF=F) this will zero out the fresh-water forcing
  for the full simulation (and not only the first time-step).

As a consequence of removing this old bug, update all 4 ADM and all 4 TLM reference output
files from reference platform "villon.mit.edu".

message:
Update ctrl_get_gen.F (#194)

* Update ctrl_get_gen.F

Originally only the first two time variable tau u and tau v control records were disabled.  We think this is because the long ago someone noticed that the optimization tends to make very large adjustments to the first one or two records for reasons that are not entirely clear.  We recently found very large adjustments in the first two control records of all of the other atmospheric controls. 

The CTRL_SKIP_FIRST_TWO_ATM_REC_ALL option simply extends the original logic applied to tau u and tau v fields to all the time variable atmospheric controls.

* few edits (less duplicated code)
  also remove trailing blanks and double consecutive blank lines

* Update ctrl_get_gen.F
  moved tauu and tauv lines next to each other
  changed CPP name to CTRL_SKIP_FRIST_TWO_ATM_REC_ALL

* Document new CPP option in CTRL_OPTIONS.h

* Update optfile for gfortran v10

- with recent version of gfortran (version 10.*), need to have special option
  "-fallow-argument-mismatch" to avoid stopping when compiling src files that
  contain multiple routine calls with 1 argument beeing of different type between
  calls (in this case, the type of argument depends on value of an other argument).
  This is very common with MPI subroutine calls and difficult to avoid when most
  of S/R are in the same file (e.g., ad_taf_output.f).
- Try to get the compiler version leading number and only add option above
  for compiler version 10 or higher.

* Remove verbose flag "-v" from default mpirun command

In testreport, the mpirun "-v" flag has been removed in Dec 2015 ; however,
it's still here in "do_tst_2+2" default mpirun command and, less used, in tst_2+2
script. Remove this flag from both scripts (consistent with testreport).

* Improve how to get compiler version

Thanks to @jahn, use a more robust and better way to get the compiler
leading version number.

* fix small issue #419

As discussed in issue #419, the "nf-config" call is, at the end "safe" (since
we check for return value in second part of the test, even when command is
not found, the logic works as expected) but a bit annoying (error message).
By re-directing the error to /dev/null, the annoying message (if any) is gone.

Also update a little bit the comments at the top of this optfile.

* update comments related to engaing MPI settings

* Document update of linux_amd64_gfortran optfile

author: Alistair Adcroft <aadcroft@princeton.edu>
message:
New package for controlling termination of the model based on the wall clock:
This is handy for those of us who keep losing 5000 cpuhours because the model
took 5 minutes longer than it did the day before.

To use:
 In package.conf, add   runclock
 In data.pkg, add       useRunClock=.TRUE.
 Add data.runclock to read
    &RUNCLOCK
    RC_maxtime_hr=2,
    RC_maxtime_mi=30,
    RC_maxtime_sc=0,
    &

The package also write the delta Wall Clock between each model step.
Who can explain a 30% slow down after 60 iterations? Who even knew about it?
Now you can find out lots of dark secrets about the EM EYE TEE GEE SEE EM...

author: Alistair Adcroft <aadcroft@princeton.edu>
message:
Added PTRACERS package

This allows an arbitrary number of passive tracers to be integrated
forward simultaneously with the dynamicaly model.
 + Implemented so far:
    - basic forward algorithm (time-stepping, advection, diffusion, convection)
    - I/O and checkpointing
    - GM/Redi  *but*  using the GM/Redi coefficient of Salt
 + Not implemented so far:
    - KPP
    - OBCS
 + No specific example supplied (yet) but global_ocean.90x40x15 has the
   necessary data.ptracer file. Simply use -enable=ptracers and uncomment
   line in data.pkg. PTRACER01 then reproduces Salt exactly.
 + This package is disabled by default since it increases storage.

message:
store directives in gad_advection (#611)

* store variables only on local tapes in gad_advection

avoid unnecessary recomputations, but recompute full routine (only)
once in ad-routine. This saves a lot of memory at the cost of a single
recomputation, but with previous store directives there were
recomputations anyway. This change changes results when
useApproxAdvectionInAdMode=.TRUE., because now all tapes are computed
with inAdMode=.TRUE., before, this was a random mix of tapes with
inAdMode=.False. and local recomputations with inAdMode=.true.

* consistent indentation

* small cleanup, remove unnecessary code and comments

* fix store directives also for GAD_MULTDIM_COMPRESSIBLE

* Update output after switching storage dir in GAD_ADVECTION

quoting PR description: with useApproxAdvectionInAdMode=.True., now all tapes are
computed with inAdMode=.True. whereas before, there was a random mix of tapes with
inAdMode=.False. and local recomputations with inAdMode=.True.

* rename local tapes and simplify use of DISABLE_MULTIDIM_ADVECTION

- one ifndef DISABLE_MULTIDIM_ADVECTION removes all code in this
  routine
- rename from gad_advtape to loctape_gad_adv, longer name requires
  some extra line breaks

- add a useless "STOP" when DISABLE_MULTIDIM_ADVECTION is defined
- fix minor typo in error msg

* bring back af-field and copy it to afx or afy to unbreak diagnostics

* remove factor nthreads_chkpt as it is always 1

* remove factor nthreads_chkpt as it is always 1

* add a comment, change an (arbitray) value and fix formatting

* minor adjustemnt to previous changes

* add a line to make sure that I get the blame

* simplify (fix) key computation, remove (now) unused parameters

* another small change

* fix for case ALLOW_TAMC_CHECKPOINTING undef

* use new format of cleaned-up tamc.h

* test experiment without tamc checkpointing

* simplify (fix?) key computations in model/src/*.F files

* simplify (fix?) key computations in all pkgs

* make a store directive short to fit the 72 character limit

interestin bug: all of "isbyte" ran beyond the 72 character limit, so
that TAF just saw 69 characters:
CADJ STORE recip_eta_qrNM1 = comlev1_cg2d_iter, key = icg2dkey, byte =
just used the default precision and did not complain. But we want to
do it right, don't we?

* improve documentation, more adjustments

* fix 1 typo

* define and compute max_lev3/4 only when necessary

to avoid problems with potentially undefined nchklev_3 and also
consistent with defining ilev_3/4

* update tamc.h in verification other experiments

following recent refinements of pkg/autodiff/tamc.h
notes:
- AUTODIFF_4_LEVEL_CHECKPOINT not in AUTODIFF_2_LEVEL_CHECKPOINT
- AUTODIFF_4_LEVEL_CHECKPOINT is not tested in verif. experiments

* minor adjustment

- put back original value of numItersMax
- adjust comments for isbyte value

* remove some obscure comments

* put (wrong) key computation within ifdefs and add comment about it

the routine is called from gmredi_calc_tensor three times for each
level k, neither of which is taken into account with this
key. This is only relevant if GMREDI_WITH_STABLE_ADJOINT is
defined, which is the case for ECCOv4, so we add the ifdef
around the key computation.

* remove all taf-related code, as it is not necessary

* minor: avoid un-used variable

and move setting of ikey next to where it's used

* document cleaning of "tamc.h"

author: Martin Losch <Martin.Losch@awi.de>
message:
o pkg/seaice: introduce new parameter SEAICEscaleSurfStress (default = .FALSE.)
  - if TRUE scale ice-ocean and ice-atmosphere stress acting on sea ice
    by AREA according to Connelly et al. (2004), JPO.
  - For EVP and the LSR solver, the implicit part of the drag term is
    the only non-zero term in the denominator when there is no ice (which
    prevented running the model with zero ice-ocean drag). If
    SEAICEscaleSurfStress = .TRUE., this results in a division by zero
    (or zero main diagonals BU/BV) which need to be caught. A practical
    consequence is that for open water, the momentum equation reduce
    to trivially 0 = 0 + 0 (for EVP). For LSR, BU/BV are reset to 1, if
    they happen to be zero, often leading to a non-zero solution over
    open water.

author: Gael Forget <gforget@mit.edu>
message:
o pkg/ctrl: option ALLOW_PACKUNPACK_METHOD2

  provides an alternative way to handle pack/unpack in adjoint runs.
  Here we rely on commonly used, up-to-date, I/O mdsio routines
  (WRITE_REC_3D_RL.F and REC_REC_3D_RL.F) rather than on mdsio_gl.F.
  Indeed mdsio_gl.F, which is used only in pack/unpack, has not been
  thorougly maintained, which leads pack/unpack to fail in several situations.
  METHOD2 is expected to prove more robust and require less maintenance.
  It could eventually become the default. The basic testing was done
  with a a cube sphere, using exch2, multiple processors + mpi, multiple
  tiles per processor, and with discarded blank tiles. Unlike the current
  default, METHOD2 seemed to work just fine using singlecpuio or not,
  using processor sub-directories or not.

in the file to seaice_solve4temp_adx.F and the TAF store calls use
seaice_solve4temp_adx instead of seaice_solve4temp.

MITgcm_contrib/ifenty/Fenty_seaice_thermo_code_merge/reborn_c65h/code/seaice_growth.F

note: these two codes will run 'as-is'.  To invoke them, add the
following line to  SEAICE_OPTIONS.h :

seven) did not change the adjoint gradients in the 1D thermodynamic
verification experiment's 11000 time step test.

author: Alistair Adcroft <aadcroft@princeton.edu>
message:
Restructered the calling tree between THE_MODEL_MAIN()
and DYNAMICS(). Two calling levels have been inserted
to better split the "fixed" initialization phase from
the main time-loop for easier connectivity with the adjoint
infrastructure.

The calling tree now looks like:

   the_model_main:
      initialise_fixed()
      the_main_loop()

   the_main_loop:
      initialise_varia()
      do i=1,nIters
         forward_step()
      enddo
      forward_step()

   forward_step:
      load_external_fields()
      dynamics()
      do_the_model_io()
      solve_for_pressure()
      do_gterm_blocking_exchanges()
      write_checkpoint()

- the code got cleaned-up (revisions 1.71 to 1.75) while keeping results unchanged.
- the lab_sea forward verification experiments were revised, because they appeared
 to be too fragile to provide a reliable safety net. Typically, minor changes that
 should only affect truncation errors (such as the present check-in) would
 lead to complete failures (loosing ~ all digits) of lab_sea tests even on Faulks
 with g77. The revised tests seem to better discriminate between issues (see below).
 Hopefully the upcoming modifications to seaice_growth.F will further stabilize the tests...

 the ocean) from ice meters to W/m2, consistent with the other heat stocks.
 This change should only affect truncation errors.

author: An T. Nguyen <atnguyen@ices.utexas.edu>
message:
Sixth mod of pkg/iceplume, no change in results.

 - Major change to read in only one field runoffQsg (Q_sg) instead of
   two fields runoffVel (w_sg) and runoffRad (r_sg).  This is
   because, based on Tom Cowton's intention, a rate Q_sg is chosen,
   based on which w_sg is assumed to be 1.0 and r_sg is computed
   OFFLINE in matlab, then output to two 4-D arrays runoff[Vel,Rad],
   which subsequently is then read in and re-combined to produce
   runoffQsg (Q_sg) online in iceplume_calc.F . By making this mod,
   we remove the extra offline workload and hidden assumption that
   w_sg is assumed to be 1, and potential error if the offline and
   online conversions of Q_sg<-->[w,r]_sg happen to differ.

 - Add a new fixed variable wVel_sg_0, set to 1.0, to explicitly
   show the assumption of velocity, and for use to compute r_sg
   = runoffRad online.  Online runoffVel = w_sg = wVel_sg_0.

 - iceplume_tendency_apply: only cosmetic change here, not relevant
   to the Q_sg switch.

 - No change in results of atn's small test.

message:
KPP: some cleanup and regularisation (#346)

* quick fix to make option KPP_ESTIMATE_UREF work

this is not test at all but now one can at a least compile the code
when this option is defined

* improve previous fix: only pass dbloc

- integer array work1 is replaced by a scalar kTmp within
  kpp_forcing_surf.F
- local array zF = abs(rF) replaces rF in the KPP_ESTIMATE_UREF code
  to avoid negative arguments of LOG(), but also in an attempt to fix
  this code more generally

* remove a forgotten print statement

* enable KPP_ESTIMATE_UREF code for this experiment

* clean code for better efficiency

- move some k-loops out
- precompute some expensive terms (log) and divisions
- use model variables instead of reconstructing them
- avoid superfluous function calls

* fix code CPP-option KPP_ESTIMATE_UREF

- add dbloc to list of formal parameters of kpp_forcing_surf
- define variables previously undefined
- fix computation of logarithmic profile with undefined log()
- define KPP_ESTIMATE_UREF in verification/vermix (does not do
  anything to the results)

* small re-organisation and clean up

- advoid divisions by grid factors
- reorganize initialisation loops to avoid inside k-loops
- add some comments
- streamline indentation

* finish incomplete merge

* cleanup: avoid computing the same thing over and over again

* add more explanatory comments

* move another k-loop outside of i/j loops

* add two new diagnostcs and fix a masking error for dbloc

* add code that turn off matching of diffusivities and more

- add CPP-flags KPP_DO_NOT_MATCH_DIFFUSIVITIES/DERIVATIVES that allow
  turning off the matching code for diffusivities at the bottom of the
  mixed layer. This can solve noise problems within the mixed layer.
- add CPP-flag KPP_SMOOTH_REGULARISATION to turn on smooth
  regularisation of division by small numbers.
- introduce scaling of shear mixing by shear (CPP-flag
  KPP_SCALE_SHEARMIXING)
- remove one unnecessary diagnostics array
- add some comments for future reference

* fix some variable declarations as a function of new CPP-flags

* fix a bug in mixed layer depth determination

- revert the order of a k-loop to actually find the shallowest depth as
  planned and not the deepest depth where dB/dz exceeds dB_dz
- add some comments

* add suggestions for vertical averaging over zRef if zRef>drF(1)

- comment out limiting zRef to drF(1) give this code a chance
- this should smooth dVsq with KPP_ESTIMATE_UREF defined in the case
  of very high vertical resolution (only)

* replace 1 with k (=1) to be more consistent

* remove double consecutive blank lines

* minor edits

- fix a typo in modified comment.
- improve comments: list the 2 subroutines in this file ; more standard format for
  routine description ; move functions declaration after argument S/R argument list
- few lower/upper case changes (more uniform across this file).

author: Jean-Michel Campin <jmc@ocean.mit.edu>
message:
Allow to use isotropic 3D Smagorinsky diffusivity:

Smag diffusivity is assumed to be linearly dependent on 3D Smag viscosity
(just scaled by inverse of a constant Prandtl number); setting involves:
 a) CPP Option: ALLOW_SMAG_3D_DIFFUSIVITY in CPP_OPTIONS.h (def. #undef)
 b) setting smag coeff. "smag3D_diffCoeff" for diffusivity (similar to smag coeff.
   "smag3D_coeff" for viscosity) in first namelist of main parameter file "data".

Implementation:
 - computed from same place as "viscAh3d_00" (in mom_calc_smag_3d.F), stored
   in common block and located at grid-cell center.
 - simple averaging from grid-cell center to grid-cell faces is applied when
   computing diffusion fluxes.
 - diffusivity is lagging by one time-step:
   a) if staggered time-step, smag3D_diffK is not updated after velocity update
      and is applied directly to tracers.
   b) if synchronous time-step, smag3D_diffK is not updated at the beginning of
      time-step and an older diffusivity field is used to step forward tracers.
   As a consequence, smag3D_diffK needs to be stored in pickup files for a proper restart.

author: Jean-Michel Campin <jm-c@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
more Momentum options, mostly related to hFac (#809)

* New Coriolis option "selectCoriScheme = 4"

This switch allows to compute Coriolis terms, both horizontal (in 2.Omega.sin(Phi))
and NH (in 2.Omega.cos(Phi)), using the averaged transport (with face edge length
and hFac factor), as done previously in V.I. for horizontal Coriolis.

* Change vertical advection for deepAtmosphere=T

For deep-model, absorb the NH-metric terms w.(u,v)/r into vertical advection
by advecting the product "deepFac x (u,v)" (instead of just u,v).

* improve new comments

* Adjust NH coriolis (new, selectCoriScheme=4) expression

- Add recip_hFacW/S (previously commented out) in new expression
  (selectCoriScheme=4) of NH coriolis f'*W term
- remove hFacW/S from gW-Cori in selectCoriScheme=4 code and keep previous
  selectCoriScheme=4 code (with hFacW/S) under selectCoriScheme=6 block

* New Spherical Metric term expression

- New Spherical-Metric term form using grid-spacing finite differences (instead
  of analytical tan(Phi)/rSphere), supposed to improve both AM and KE conservation.
  Used (turned on) when selectVortScheme=1,2.
- Add option to absorb the spherical-metric terms uMetricTerms = u.v.tanPhi/r
  into meridional advection by advecting the product "dxC x u" (instead of just u).
  Used (turned on) when selectVortScheme=2.
Note: for now, re-cycle Flux-Form unused param "selectVortScheme" for this.

* Adjust again gW-Cori just for the case selectCoriScheme=6

This option (selectCoriScheme=6, in mom_w_coriolis_nh.F) was left from early
test, with hFacW/S multiplying uVel,vVel, but without scaling by any recip_hFac.
The changes here fix this issue as the gW-Cori term is now divided by the
grid-cell thickness at the wVel location (new argument recip_rThickC).

* Refine changes to vertical advection for deepAtmosphere=T

Two improvements:
- single CPP option "MOM_USE_OLD_DEEP_VERT_ADV" in MOM_COMMON_OPTIONS.h to
  disable changes to vertical advection for deepAtmosphere=T
- fix for the case useNHTerms=F with deepAtmosphere=T.
Done by keeping a local copy of deepFacC in MOM_VISC.h, and adding 1 new
argument to S/R mom_u_adv_wu.F, mom_v_adv_wv.F, mom_vi_{u,v}_vertshear.F

* Add new choice for vorticity advection, without r_hFacZ

This new option (with selectCortScheme=4) skip the division of vorticity
by hFacZ and replace it with tendency scaling by recip_hFacW/S
Also:
 - remove code related to "upwindVort3" (was hard-coded to FALSE)
 - add some missing "_d 0" ; + minor indentation changes

* use new parameter "select3dCoriScheme"

no need to hack selectCoriScheme params and leave mom_vi_coriolis.F unchanged

* use new parameter "selectMetricTerms"

- no need to hack selectVortScheme param
- compute advection tendency in separated block if selectMetricTerms
  This makes sure results will not be affected (at trucation level)
  with current default metric-terms.
- minor cleaning in mom_u/v_coriolis.F and mom_u/v_adv_wu/v.F

* add diagnostics for Metric-Terms tendency

* add diagnostics for Metric-Terms tendency

also rename 2 local variables (vF & v4F) more inline with other S/R
and improve description

* report new selections in config-summary

* add secondary deep-model test

using vector-invariant momentum

* Update ref. output + add new one

With deep-model, gU,gV NHMtTerms have been moved inside vertical momentum advection
and this affects results (11 remaining matching digits for cg2d); update primary test
ref. output and add ref-output for new (vector-inv) secondary test.

* add/edit new parms into ch 3 namelist tables

* switch order

* Fix missing setting of deepFacAdv

for the case where MOM_USE_OLD_DEEP_VERT_ADV is defined and useNHMTerms=F
(spotted by @owang01)

* remove un-used "metricTerms" logical

* more consistent use of "halfRL"

* document new momentum discretisation options

author: Martin Losch <30285667+mjlosch@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Fix mapping of time dependent generic control variables (gentim2d) (#380)

* replace endrec by diffrec where it makes sense

this change fixes a bug that makes it impossible to run an AD
simulation from an arbitray pickup file: This routine assumes
startrec = 1 (which is not true when starting from a pickup) and
endrec can become quite large, so that the number of records written
to fnamegenIn (in S/R ctrl_init, calls ctrl_init_ctrlvar with
diffrec->ncvarrecs which then calls ctrl_set_globfld_xy, where file is
written with ncvarrecs = diffrec records) are not enough. diffrec =
endrec-startrec+1 appears to the be correct number of records.

* remove unnecessary line

* add some documentation about the generic control variables

- append table with "xx_runoff", because it is actually defined in the
  code

* suppress writing meta files in reverse mode in adread_* files

by specifying a negative record number. This assumes that the meta
files of adxx-files (gradients with respect to controls), etc. have
been properly written in the initialisation phase and fixes a bug
where the parameter nrecords in the meta file does not correspond to
the number of records actually in the adxx-file.

* also suppress writing meta files in reverse mode in adwrite routines

* Document fix for gentim2d control variables

author: Alistair Adcroft <aadcroft@princeton.edu>
message:
Changed the order of operations for global sums of arrays.
 o this *DOES* change output
   - the following results are updated by this change:
        exp4 front_relax global_ocean.cs32x15 global_ocean_pressure
        ideal_2D_oce internal_wave natl_box plume_on_slope
   - changes are primarily due to different cg2d residuals but in some
     the Eta field changes and this changes other fields
 o the global sum used to accumulate sequentially over all tiles on a single
   process and then the result be passed to _GLOBAL_SUM()
 o now we create a sum per tile and accumulate the sums
   - this should fix differences in sum for two tiles on 1 or 2 processors
   - this may help when using more than2 tiles but is not guaranteed
   - introducing a gather operation in GLOBAL_SUM() will fix differences
     for multiple tiles but only for fixed tiles configurations
   - an array based sum function is needed to make this independent of
     tile configuration

author: Jean-Michel Campin <jmc@ocean.mit.edu>
Jean-Michel Campin <jmc@mit.edu>
message:
fix for special value of R_low with shelfice

When bathymetry field value is just rF(k)+hFacMin*drF(k)/2, R_low will deepen
 (by hFacMin*drF(k)/2 ) to satisfy the hFacMin criteria. In this case:
- if R_shelfIce value (from file) was exactly equal to initial bathymetry depth,
  original code would create a very thin grid cell of thickness factor hFacMin.
  Fix this problem by preventing deepening of R_low when initial R_low >= R_shelfIce.
- if R_shelfIce value is deeper than original value, the problem does not
  show up for hFacC (column remains dry) but because of erronous resetting
  of rSurfW/S (to be the MAX of rSurfW/S, rLowW/S) this could trigger the same
  type of artifical deepening at Western and Sourthern column edges (for hFacW
  and hFacS). Remove early resetting of rSurfW/S to fix this second issue.

author: Constantinos Evangelinos <constantinos.evangelinos@gmail.com>
message:
Added calls to initialize and finalize the HPM Toolkit for performance
counters (currently working under AIX and Linux/PPC). One sets the
environment variable HPM_EVENT_SET to a value 1(default)-4 for Power3 systems
and 0-60(default) for Power4. All sections timed by calls to timer_start
and timer_stop would also be monitored for the specified event set. If the
number of monitored sections is more than 100 then the environment variable
HPM_NUM_INST_PTS needs to be adjusted appropriately. In the case of multi-
threaded code there cannot be more than 99 timed sections and HPM_NUM_INST_PTS
should be adjusted to 100*(#_of_threads -1). At the end of the code's
execution the HPM Toolkit generates a set of files hpm*.viz and perfhpm*.*
that can be further analyzed. For more information look at
http://www.research.ibm.com/actc/projects/hardwareperf2.shtml
Currently needs to have declared HPMTINC and HPMTLIB in the optfile for
the include and library linking strings needed to use HPMT.

this change fixes a bug that makes it impossible to run an AD
simulation from an arbitray pickup file: This routine assumes
startrec = 1 (which is not true when starting from a pickup) and

to fnamegenIn (in S/R ctrl_init, calls ctrl_init_ctrlvar with
diffrec->ncvarrecs which then calls ctrl_set_globfld_xy, where file is
written with ncvarrecs = diffrec records) are not enough. diffrec =
endrec-startrec+1 appears to the be correct number of records.

message:
modify Stevens boundary conditions so that S/R obcs_calc_stevens
computes tendency for temperature and salinity that is then applied to
update theta and salt in S/R obcs_apply_ts; this requires proper
masking of all horizontal advection and diffusion contributions on the
boundary (in S/Rs gad_advection, gad_calc_rhs, gmredi_rtransport,
gmredi_calc_diff), and removing the mask in S/R timestep_tracer. The
advantage of this approach is that the updated tracer values include
contributions from the surface forcing and vertical diffusion. This
modification changes exp4.stevens because of vertical diffusion.

for now this is a hack, because the new routines just convert fields

real*8 fields.
use RS interface for many RS fields (e.g. forcing fields, to be
tested) of the main code (no fields from packages yet).

* use RS tapes for RS variables in packages, where I could find them

* remove obsolete comments and adjust remaining part

* Revert "use RS tapes for RS variables in packages, where I could find them"

This reverts commit 33fd3013b0269a3ea6c126ff7939b259daacac1c.

* Revert "add interface for RS variables and fix INT interface"

This reverts commit 36f31234882d727c5bc10cf39b60e03e05d4613d.

* reinsert code lost in the reverts, add comment, fix integer code

replace dynamic array allocation by static array allocation
anticipating a 2D array, stop if length of field does not match.

* rename integer routines and move to a separate new file

adiread and adiwrite are renamed to adread_i and adwrite_i

* fix few comments

Some comment updates from PR #498 got lost in the merge. Put them back.

* remove few space/blanks

Just to have more consistency.

* Simplify + more robust:

- use compiler type conversion for Integer to Real*8 instead of "FLOAT"
  (which results in 2 conversions, from Int to real*4 and then to real*8,
   with (unlikely) risk of round-off when converting large integer);
- do not stop when length is smaller than size of local 2-D array (it should
  just works fine);

author: Ian G Fenty <Ian.Fenty@jpl.nasa.gov>
message:
Fixed 2 bugs in seaice_growth.F

Bug 1: calculation of saltFlux (and saltPlumeFlux) by removing dependence on now-defunct parameter ICE2WATR.
and slightly simplifying the equation.  Now if the sea ice salinity equals the local seawater salinity, the growth of sea ice
will not alter the seawater salinity.

old equation:
           saltFlux(I,J,bi,bj) =
       &            HEFFM(I,J,bi,bj)/SEAICE_deltaTtherm
       &            *SEAICE_salinity*salt(I,j,kSurface,bi,bj)
!      &            *tmpscal1*ICE2WATR*rhoConstFresh

new equation:
           saltFlux(I,J,bi,bj) =
       &            HEFFM(I,J,bi,bj)/SEAICE_deltaTtherm
       &            *SEAICE_salinity*salt(I,j,kSurface,bi,bj)
!      &            *tmpscal1*SEAICE_rhoIce

As ICE2WATR equaled SEAICE_rhoICE/rhoConst and not SEAICE_rhoICE/rhoConstFresh, verification experiments where
rhoConstFresh did not equal rhoConst need to be updated.

Bug 2: replaced hFacC with maskC in the calculation of the turbulent ocean-ice flux (found by Gael) (doesn't change results).

author: ifenty <ifenty@gmail.com>
message:
Seventh version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes.

This version of seaice_growth_adx.F builds on version six.  It includes
Arash Bigdeli's improvements for properly handling freshwater fluxes
when the model is configured with a nonlinear free surface in
seaice_growth_adx.F, including the cases when negative values of heff
are passed to seaice_growth_adx.F after seaice advection.  There are
also new diagnostic terms to allow offline budget closure.  Salt plume
codes that had been removed in version six are added back in here.

note: this code will run 'as-is'  to invoke them use the line
in SEAICE_OPTIONS.h

This version of the code was compared against version six and had
identical gradients in the 1D_ocean_ice_column verification experiment
11000 time step test without salt plume defined.

author: Martin Losch <30285667+mjlosch@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Fix treatment of viscFacAdj for vector-invariant momentum code (#384)

* add a new runtime parameter viscFacInFw

This runtime parameter can be used to adjust viscFacAdj also in
forward mode in analogy to viscFacInAd for the AD-mode.

* remove some (hopefully) unnecessary store directives

- the main part is not storing viscAh/4_D/Z, so that they are
  explicitly recomputed in mom_vecinv_ad.f. This is necessary for the
  viscFacAdj to have an effect on the AD simulations
- this does not change the number of recomputation warnings

* introduce CPP directive AUTODIFF_ALLOW_VISCFACADJ

- define this flag to be able to use viscFacAdj via viscFacInAd/Fw
- reintroduce storing of viscAh/4_D/Z in mom_vecinf, if flag not defined
- add a minimal test: stop if viscFacInAd/Fw set, but CPP flag not defined
- test compilation of this code in tutorial_global_oce_optim

* add viscFacAdj also to viscosity as Z-points

- not sure why this was not part of the original code

* improve WARNING messages if parameters are insufficently specified

* enable ALLOW_3D_VISCAH to make this experiment work

- add forgotting file

* comment out viscFacInAd and add an explanation of this parameter

- did not do anything anyway because 3D viscosity fields are not
  specified in this experiment.

* Document fixing and improving viscFacAdj

Add this:

  - rename TAF common block tapes to be more consistent and remove
    unnecessary duplicates
  - add store directives to remove more recomputations,
    but use smaller tapes (and adjust keys) when
    SEAICE_LSR_ADJOINT_ITER is undefined. The idea behind this flag is
    to reduce the memory footprint when the adjoint of the LSR is not

message:
seaice LSR bug fix (#369)

* fix a small bug: replace OLy by OLx

* fix the iteration for SEAICEnonLinIterMax > 2

This fixes a bug that made the iteration solve the stationary momentum
equations (i.e. du/dt -> 0) for SEAICEnonLinIterMax > 2. Thanks to
Martin Vancoppenole for pointing this out to me. For the default
SEAICEnonLinIterMax = 2, this change has no effect and all previous
simulations with this default value are unchanged.

* move fixed contribution of du/dt back into nl-loop

this is necessary to maintain results of two experiments,
not clear why. The program logic calls for the previous
version and I might revert to it and update the experiments
instead.

* replace I,J by i,j

* change time level again

* addtional store directives suppress new warnings

* replace loops with full loop ranges by array assignments

* Remove array operations again as we do not like them.

* Minor switch that does affect results @ truncation level.

In preparation for moving all "fixed" terms (i.e., kept the same during non-linear solver loop)
into FORCEX0,FORCEY0, switch the order of increment to FORCEX,FORCEY by adding time-derivative
contribution before ocean-drag (vs after coriolis term as previously done).
Note: This does affect results at manchine truncation level.

* Update output of experiments that use seaice LSR

Results change (at machine truncation level) because of different
ordering of additions to FORCEX,FORCEY in seaice_lsr.F

* Finally: move time derivative contribution to rhs out of iteration

This is a cleaner solution and involves few operations.

* leave FORCEX/Y0 untouched by seaice_lsr and add store directives

this also advoids TAF recomputation warnings

* Document bug-fix in seaice_lsr.F for SEAICEnonLinIterMax>2

author: Constantinos Evangelinos <constantinos.evangelinos@gmail.com>
message:
Introduce runtime floating point control into MITgcm using the GSL.
main.F calls fgsl_ieee_env_setup (), a wrapper around gsl_ieee_env_setup ()
from the GNU Scientific Library which reads in the environment
variable GSL_IEEE_MODE and sets the environment accordingly. For
more information look at:
http://www.gnu.org/software/gsl/manual/gsl-ref_39.html#SEC515
Please read this carefully to avoid running into trouble with exceptions
due to denormals and underflows.
gsl_ieee_env.c provides fgsl_ieee_env_setup () in multiple forms that
should be recognized by any fortran compiler.
Currently needs to have declared GSLINC and GSLLIB in the optfile
for the include and library linking strings needed to use GSL.
For example on most Linux boxen
GSLINC=''
GSLLIB='-lgsl -lgslcblas'
as the required files exist in /usr/include and /usr/lib.

message:
Update matlab cs grid scripts (#729)

* Update to also work with compact-format input

New: change grid-point ordering when stored in a long vector, to always be consistent with
     compact-format (i.e., one face after an other)

* Allow to work with compact format input

Also rename scalHV_colbar.m to moveHV_colbar.m (was already used in grph_CS.m)

* Update (+simplify) "mk_psiLine.m"

Consistent with (new) convention for long-vector storage (like comapct format,
one face after an other). Also compatible with both compact-format and original
format for input files.

* New script to generate "broken-lines"

Use a different (and simpler) method to find broken-lines for Meridional Transp.
Strean-Function than the matlab-scripts in dir "bk_line".
This method is based on tagging grid-cell center according to latitude position
relative to target-latitude vector "yLat"; and then collecting the interface
edges (i.e., velocity grid-point) that separate 2 adjacent center grid-cell
with a jump in tag value across the corresponding latitude target.

Also add an example script that computes Merid. Transp. Stream-Function.

* Update content

* Updated for compact-format input

* Update "rgbDim" to match pkg/exch2 meaning

Also allow 6-facets input field.

- update nR,nG,nB to match pkg/exch2 convention ; adopt same "facet" identifier

all calling the same master-thread global-sum routine (acting on

that fit into fixed buffer sice "GSVec_size".

and move new param "GSVec_size" inside EEPARAMS.h

Also remove, in EEPARAMS.h, commented out (since Feb 2014) params:

author: Gael Forget <gforget@mit.edu>
message:
Merging seaice_growth codes -- part 3 -- the merging, at last.

- introducing HEFFpreTH, HSNWpreTH, and AREApreTH that allows the switch from the 'legacy' code to
  the 'merged' code. In 'legacy' HEFFpreTH=HEFFnm1 (pre adv-diff), HSNWpreTH=hsnow (post adv-diff),
  AREApreTH=areanm1 (pre adv-diff), while HEFF/HSNOW/ARE (post adv-diff) are the stocks that get
  updated by seaice-growth.F, and we treat pathological cases along the way, and at the end
  mostly (after all thermo updates, but for the flooding).
- in the 'merged' way, we start with post-advection HEFF/HSNOW/AREA, treat pathological cases
  at once, and use the result (a self-consistent HEFF/HSNOW/AREA set) as our starting point.
- the CPP switch is SEAICE_GROWTH_LEGACY, which for now is hard-coded to #define.

author: An T. Nguyen <atnguyen@ices.utexas.edu>
message:
add ifdef LAYERS_DIAG_TOTTEND and logical layers_diag_tottendTS

The values for tottend[T,S] are calculated when
(1) diagnostics of tottend[T,S] are requested outside of pkg/layers
AND/OR
(2) diagnostics of tottend[T,S] are requested INSIDE pkg/layers.
In case of (2) inside pkg/layers, prior to being diagnosed, the
tottend variables are being passed around as input arguments for
subroutines layers_calc.F and layers_fluxcalc.F, prior to the final
diagnostic call. Here, we introduce (a) option LAYERS_DIAG_TOTTEND
in LAYERS_OPTIONS.h (default to #define) to strip all array definitions,
subroutine arguments, and related calculations, thus saving memory
and computed time, and (b) logical "layers_diag_tottendTS" (default
to .TRUE.) to allow the filling of the layers diagnotics.

author: Michael Bates <m.bates@griffith.edu.au>
message:
Changes associated with the PV eddy closure (GM_K3D) include:
o To improve efficiency the call to solve for the eigenvectors only happen once every GM_K3D_vecFreq seconds.  This required the following changes:
  - read and write pickup files for the eigenvectors and deformation radius (gmredi_read_pickup.F and gmredi_write_pickup.F)
  - making the number of modes (GM_K3D_NModes) a parameter which must be specified at compile time in GMREDI.h
  - A new namelist variable, GM_K3D_vecFreq
  - Added modesC, modesW, modesS and Rdef to the common block
o If the CPP option use_lapack is undefined, then a WKB approximation to the eigenvectors and deformation radius is now used (although, it seems unstable; so for the moment an error is raised in gmredi_check if GM_K3D is defined but use_lapack is not).
o Changed gmredi_calc_eigs returns the deformation radius rather than the deformation wavenumber
o Fixed bug in calculation of tfluxX and tfluxY for the instance where the surface layer is the depth of the water column.
o Added warning messages if there are problems with calculating eigenmodes and eigenvectors
o Cleaned up code
o Improved documentation
o Rationalised diagnostics
o Added some extra startup checks (gmredi_check)
