message:
Fix r* pressure gradient for oceanic case where r @ top <> 0

The r* coordinate sloping term was following the 2004 paper, which only
consider the case where the model top is at r == 0 (Z-coord: Ro_surf == 0 everywhere
and P-coord: R_low == 0 everywhere).

Fix sloping term expression for the general case (P or Z coordinate) but, for now,
only use general expression when r @ top is known to be not uniformly zero (either
because origign seaLev_Z / top_Pres is non zero or when allowing cavities: useShelfice
or using topoFile).

Note: could use general form for all cases but this affects results at machine truncation level

author: jm-c <jm-c@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Allows to skip check fc part in genmake2 (#209)

* Adjust FC check implementation to enable to skip the check.
  Enable to skip the "check_fortran_compiler" part by setting
  (e.g., in optfile) FC_CHECK to anything else than 't'.

* Disable "Check for Fortran Compiler" part in  optfile: linux_ia64_cray_archer:
  It turns out that the running test part does not ever terminate when tried on
  compute node; the reason beeing related to (hard to use) mpiexec:
From Archer Helpdesk Team:
  When running on a login node, there is no mpiexec. When running on a PP node,
  there is, in /opt/pbs/12.2.401.141761/bin/mpiexec. This runs a user-supplied mpiexec,
  and tries to not run itself (in an infinite recursion) but fails because it compares
  the strings /opt/pbs/default/bin (where PBS thinks the bin directory is) and
  /opt/pbs/12.2.401.141761/bin (the directory in PATH). This is an error in the PBS
  script (or in Archer's configuration).
By setting: FC_CHECK=f in optfile, the whole "Check for Fortran Compiler"
is skipped.

* document option to skip check FC part in genmake2

author: Constantinos Evangelinos <constantinos.evangelinos@gmail.com>
message:
Added calls to use either the HPM Toolkit or the PAPI library to further
instrument for performance counter monitoring the sections timed with
timer_start and timer_stop calls. The PAPI calls currently are not
thread-safe and will not work with OpenMP. To use PAPI one needs to
have a file data.papi in the working directory with the following format:
n
PAPI_EVENT_1
PAPI_EVENT_2
...
PAPI_ENENT_n
where the available PAPI event names on a given platform can be found using
the "avail" PAPI utility. Please note that not all events can be monitored
at the same time and that each platform has a maximum number of event
counters. One may use the papi_events.F utility in contrib to generate a
valid data.papi. The PAPI numbers are printed at the end of execution along
the standard timing numbers. PAPI and HPMT monitoring cannot co-exist. For
more information about PAPI please look at:
http://icl.cs.utk.edu/papi/

author: Alistair Adcroft <aadcroft@princeton.edu>
message:
Changed the order of operations for global sums of arrays.
 o the global sum used to accumulate sequentially over all tiles on a single
   process and then the result be passed to _GLOBAL_SUM()
 o now we create a sum per tile and accumulate the sums
   - this should fix differences in sum for two tiles on 1 or 2 processors
   - this may help when using more than2 tiles but is not guaranteed
   - introducing a gather operation in GLOBAL_SUM() will fix differences
     for multiple tiles but only for fixed tiles configurations
   - an array based sum function is needed to make this independent of
     tile configuration

author: Gael Forget <gforget@mit.edu>
message:
Merging seaice_growth codes -- part 3 -- the merging, at last.

This check-in completes the overall 10/2010 revision and merging process, by

- adding a header that explains unit/sign/naming conventions.
- introducing areaMax parameter that is, for now, hardcoded to 1.
- re-including the 'vintage bug' as a comment -- in case I got it wrong.
- bracketing 'IF (useRelativeWind)' with '#ifdef ALLOW_ATM_WIND'
  consistent with what pkg/exf does.
- merging the '_if.F' features that differ from what is in legacy code:
   - option to actually grow ice over open water, which legacy code
     only virtually takes into account in the area tendency (I think).
   - let melting by ocean reduce area (as melting by atm alone does in legacy).
   - different criteria for rain->snow (incl. as comments).

The added features are bracketed out of legacy code, so this
revision did not affect forward results. A couple cosmetic modifications
changed adjoint results by only three digits. I will only update those.

* With pkg/thsice, prevent seaice to form where there is an ice-shelf
  In case of thin ice-shelf (all in surface level => hFacC(k=1) > 0),
  need to prevent seaice to get there; modify hOceMxL accordingly.

  Reset short-wave to zero where there is an ice-shelf:
  In case of thin ice-shelf (all in surface level => hFacC(k=1) > 0),
  short-wave was not reset to zero over Ice-Shelf and was able to
  warm-up ocean below the ice-shelf (with #define SHORTWAVE_HEATING).
 Also, for consistent diagnostics, also reset Qnet to zero there.

author: ifenty <ifenty@gmail.com>
message:
Second version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F +
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from Summer
2010.  They were used for experiments showing the importance of positive
surface buoyancy forcing from melting sea ice that is advected south
over the Labrador Sea in Fenty 2010 Thesis and the Fenty and Heimbach
2012b paper.

The '_adx' suffix is chosen to indicate that these routines are useful
for adjoint calculations.

note: these two codes will not run 'as-is'  they are included here to
be part of the seaice_growth_adx.F evolution record.

author: Alistair Adcroft <aadcroft@princeton.edu>
message:
Added new parameter: deltaTfreesurf

Previously, the free-surface equation was intergrated forward
synchronously with the momentum equations. It is more consistent
to use the tracer time-step. This increases the number of
iterations required but strengthens the damping.

We *SHOULD* make the default time-step equal to the tracer time-step.
However, we don't for backward compatibility. At some point in the
future we need to change the default behaviour.

It turns out that the reason for the "reduced stability" encountered
in large-scale runs seems to be related to excess variability in
the free surface which in turn happens when the waves aren't damped.
Using a longer time-step fixes this.

author: Gael Forget <gforget@mit.edu>
message:
o eesup and pkg/mdsio: ALLOW_WHIO

  Option to write/read 2D fields to files including tiles halos.
  The main purpose is for adjoint related "tape I/O".
  The secondary purpose is for debugging phases.

  A word on those rather specifically intended purposes.
  The code was meant to be stripped down to the bare minimum.
  Typically, there is a unique and basic mapping to the global
  buffer (tile by tile, then proc by proc, then level by level), and
  byteswaps and meta-files are omitted. Indeed the (*_WH*) code is not
  meant to generate user friendly outputs of various shapes and forms.
  Rather it is intended, for the knowledgeabale developers,
  to be largely independent of the many mdsio options, to allow
  outputs of tiles+halos in debugging phases and in adjoint runs,
  and to allow some flexibility in tuning (adoint) I/O depending on each
  file system behavior. With regard to tuning, most of the potential knobs
  (to leave files open, to allocate the I/O indep. of usesinglecpuio,
  to specify directories, to specify the typical size of I/O calls, etc.)
  are not yet included, and will be added if they prove useful.

author: jm-c <jm-c@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
A hack to fix the "-nocat4ad" option with new version of TAF (#208)

* A hack to fix the "-nocat4d" option with new version of TAF

With new version of TAF (currently 4.2.7), *.flowdir files are now
assumed to be free-format source files (since they don't have either .f
or .F suffix); Up to version 4.1.1 they were assumed to be fixed format.

And when using "-nocat4d" option, we send all individual files to TAF
(instead of a single file: ad_input_code.f); so we need to explicitly
add the "-fixed" option to the TAF command to get the *.flowdir processed
correctly.

in tag-index, add document about his fix in genmake2 option "-nocat4ad"

author: Jean-Michel Campin <jm-c@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Fix ocean r* grad-P (case r @ top <>0) (#655)

* Fix r* pressure gradient for oceanic case where r @ top <> 0

The r* coordinate sloping term was following the 2004 paper, which only
consider the case where the model top is at r == 0 (Z-coord: Ro_surf == 0 everywhere
and P-coord: R_low == 0 everywhere).

Fix sloping term expression for the general case (P or Z coordinate) but, for now,
only use general expression when r @ top is known to be not uniformly zero (either
because origign seaLev_Z / top_Pres is non zero or when allowing cavities: useShelfice
or using topoFile).

Note: could use general form for all cases but this affects results at machine truncation level

* new reference output

After fixing bug in z* pressure-grad for the case model top not uniformly at z*=0,
generate new ref output (on villon, gfortran with -devel) since this test exp.
use z* under ice-shelf (only 4 remaining matching digits for cg2d).

* document fixing r* pressure gradient (case top not @ r=0)

author: Ian Fenty <ifenty@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Adjointable Sea Ice Thermodynamics: part deux (#242)

* Preliminary files required for the new seaice adjoint codes:

Includes
1. adding seaice_growth_adx.F, seaice_solve4temp_adx.F to seaice_ad_diff.list
2. adding calls to seaice_growth_adx.F in seaice_model.F
3. adding new seaice parameters to SEAICE_PARAMS.h and SEAICE_readparms.
4. adding new adjoint/forward run dependent seaice parameters to autodiff files

* First version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from spring
2010.  They were used for the state estimation work in the Fenty 2010
Ph.D. thesis and the Fenty and Heimbach 2012a paper.

The '_adx' suffix is chosen to indicate that these routines are useful for adjoint calculations.

Note: these two codes (and up to 5th version) will not run 'as-is'  they are included here to
be part of the seaice_growth_adx.F evolution record.

* Second version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from Summer
2010.  They were used for experiments showing the importance of positive
surface buoyancy forcing from melting sea ice that is advected south
over the Labrador Sea in Fenty 2010 Thesis and the Fenty and Heimbach 2012b paper.

* Third set of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from winter
2010/2011 and were created to integrate the Fenty sea ice codes with the
MITgcm main branch.  MIT folks decided to rewrite the seaice_growth.F
instead and so from then on the Fenty seaice growth codes lived quiet
and peaceful lives in the MITgcm contrib directory
/MITgcm_contrib/ifenty/Fenty_seaice_thermo_code_merge/code_update

* Fourth set of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F
codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from Jan 2013.
Codes taken from
MITgcm_contrib/ifenty/Fenty_Thermo_Code_Updates/code_updates_20130122/

* Fifth version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from early 2015.

They were not stored in /contrib but from a personal subversion repository 
of Fenty.  They appear to be the first of the 'reborn' versions.

Codes taken from /Users/ifenty/Work/poise/ModelConfigurations/branches/MergingMyIceGrowthCodeToCurrentMITgcm/SeaIceGrowthReborn

Note: these two codes (and earlier version) will not run 'as-is'  they are included here to
be part of the seaice_growth_adx.F evolution record.

* Sixth version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F code

This seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) is from sometime after early 2015.

Apparently this version of the Fenty seaice_growth code was the starting
point for  Arash Bigdeli.  The seaice_solve4temp_adx.F code is
structually the same as version 5.  Here the subroutine name is changed
in the file to seaice_solve4temp_adx.F and the TAF store calls use
seaice_solve4temp_adx instead of seaice_solve4temp.

Codes from
MITgcm_contrib/ifenty/Fenty_seaice_thermo_code_merge/reborn_c65h/code/seaice_growth.F

Note: these two codes (and later version) will run 'as-is'.
To invoke them, add the following line to  SEAICE_OPTIONS.h :

They were used to validate that the changes made by Bigdeli (version
seven) did not change the adjoint gradients in the 1D thermodynamic
verification experiment's 11000 time step test.

* Seventh version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes.

This version of seaice_growth_adx.F builds on version six.  It includes
Arash Bigdeli's improvements for properly handling freshwater fluxes
when the model is configured with a nonlinear free surface in
seaice_growth_adx.F, including the cases when negative values of heff
are passed to seaice_growth_adx.F after seaice advection.  There are
also new diagnostic terms to allow offline budget closure.  Salt plume
codes that had been removed in version six are added back in here.

This version of the code was compared against version six and had
identical gradients in the 1D_ocean_ice_column verification experiment
11000 time step test without salt plume defined.

* seaice_model.F: define bi,bj,i,j without TAMC
  the addition of a sea ice load calculation in seaice_growth requires
  bi,bj,i, and j which were previously required only when TAMC was defined.
  Now these counters are always defined.

* Cleaning:
- remove tabs, trailing blank, and double consecutive blank lines
- remove CVS Header and Name in seaice_solve4temp_adx.F

* remove storage directive for heffm:
  Martin removed all storage directives of HEFFM as part of PR #174
  since they are no longer needed. Curiously, these 2 (added back)
  storage dir trigger an additional TAF recomputation warning in experiment
  global_ocean.cs32x15 and offline_exf_seaice ; decide to remove/clean this
  with no impact on model results.

* Update SEAICE_OPTIONS.h
  Add a CPP option for turning on the adjointable sea ice thermodynamic output.  

The new SEAICE_OPTIONS.h now has an #undef placeholder fo rthe new CPP option
#undef ALLOW_SEAICE_GROWTH_ADX

* Remove trailing blanks
* document addition of adjointable seaice thermo.

replace hardwired local filename length 80 by MAX_LEN_FNAM (#715)

* replace hardwired length 80 by MAX_LEN_FNAM for local filenames

- first attempt, mostly by appling these sed commands locally:
sed -i.bak 's/(80)/(MAX_LEN_FNAM)/g' *.F
sed -i.bak 's/( 80)/(MAX_LEN_FNAM)/g' *.F
sed -i.bak 's/(80a)/(a)/g' *.F
sed -i.bak 's/(1:80)//g' *.F
with some fine tuning "by hand". I excluded all diagnostics related
declarations (diagTitle etc.), local filenames (e.g. pickups) for
which it is safe to use 80 characters, unclear usage (e.g. in fizhi),
pkg/admtlm (altogether), and pkg/atm_ocn_coupler (because none of the
files include EEPARAMS.h where MAX_LEN_FNAM is defined).

* remove (most) unnecessary initialisations of local fname

author: Gael Forget <gforget@mit.edu>
message:
- switch to HO = 0.2
  To be better consistent with thsice and initial condition.
  With SEAICE_areaLossFormula = 1, HO has a large influence on
  the ~ equilibrium solution. The three terms of melt/growth
  act separately on ice concentration, which stays below 1.
- switch to SEAICE_areaLossFormula = 2
  Leads to a ~ equilibrium solution (after 3 years run)
  that is ~1 for ice concentration (in cold atm sector)
  similar to the thsice solution.
- switch to SEAICE_growMeltByConv = .TRUE.
  Has little influence with SEAICE_areaLossFormula = 2
- switch to SEAICE_doOpenWaterMelt = .TRUE.
  Has little influence with SEAICE_areaLossFormula = 2
  over most of the domain. But there were spurious 500m ice
  in the extreme cold part of the domain (top right corner,
  where the ocean is below freezing) that are
  removed when using SEAICE_doOpenWaterMelt.
- these parameter choices do not seem to affect
  the adjoint accuracy much.

author: Patrick Heimbach <heimbach@mit.edu>
message:
Modifs to genmake2 and adjoint_default to enable mixed .f .f90 with TAF (#709)

* * We want to be able to add to TAF_COMMON_FLAGS via genmake_local
* changes to genmake2 to enable mixed .F and .F90 code for TAF

* make genmake2 work again with case-insensitive file system

- on MacOS, file systems are case-insensitive by default; we solve
that by using different file extensions for preprocessed files (.for
and .fr9); with TAF version 5.8.0 and higher, we can specify both
fixed and free format files at the command line with appropriate
flags; this also require an update of the staf script
- add more lines to remove from preprocess files before sending them
to taf.

* revert change to allow TAF_COMMON_FLAGS in genmake_local

This functionality is fully covered by TAF_EXTRA or the genmake2
command-line flag -taf_extra. For clarity, I would like to avoid an
additional redundant option

* introduce NON_AD_F90_SRC_FILES (currently empty) to make it work

for Linux and example geos_bulkformulae/global_ocean.cs32x15 of
git@github.com:christophernhill/gmao_mitgcm_couplng.git

* combine F77 and F90 ad_list files

* remove to additional comments, a change saved for later

* back to 2 $TMP files

* simplify alternative suffix replacement

* fix bug in suffix test

* Account for Martin's suggestions

* do not apply adjoint_sed to free-format f90-files

remove ad_input_code.$FS90 because it does not work (for now)

* make it work also without -ncad, add some -fixed to $(TAF) commands

The -fixed is necessary, because it is no longer included in
$(TAF_EXTRA).

* it is safer to not remove comments for AD_F90FILES for now

until we have an f90-version of remove_comments_sed that does not
accidentally remove lines starting with "C" (which is not a comment in
free-format files)

* modify tutorial_global_oce_optim to test mixed free and fixed format

- first attempt

* adjust comments

F90 elements do not work with TAF when -f77 is specified, that's why
in this file, we do not use any F90 features (except for the free
format)

* fix 2 "test -z" conditions

* change names, revert NON_AD_F90_SRC_FILES to F90_SRC_FILES for ftl

ad_input_code_f90 -> ad_inpF90_code
ad_taf_output_f90 -> ad_taf_outpF90

* simplify (ad_inpF90_code.f90 only if needed)

this avoid fake/un-used target when AD_F90FILES is empty

* revert ftlobjfiles, remove F90_SRC_FILES from target depend

- ftlobjfiles can be fixed together with all other ftl-related targets
in a separate PR
- incuding F90_SRC_FILES into the $(MAKEDEPEND) comman leads to wrong
dependencies; this needs to be fixed in a separate PR, and we leave
the f90 files for now without propert dependency lists

* Revert "adjust comments"

This reverts commit 3b829f4e314cf444a08de3a1acea570c04904cb9.

* Revert "modify tutorial_global_oce_optim to test mixed free and fixed format"

This reverts commit 1b116d850bc623bdb5bdc7b5dc3c36a3ebf7286b.

* document changes for TAF to process a mix of src

author: Jean-Michel Campin <jm-c@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Small ecco cleaning (#549)

* small changes for more robust results

- change "facNum" expression to be consistent with comment in src code:
  "facNum is 1 divided by the number of tiles in SIZE dot h"
  by adding number of tile in X per proc (i.e., nSx);
- also change "facNum" from a parameter to just a local var (some compiler do not
  accept division in parameter definition) and compute it in double precision.
- similar double precision change for "facCost"
- small cleaning: remove copies itlo,ithi,jtlo,jthi ; identation ; remove wrong
  S/R name in S/R description ; few lower/upper case changes.

* fix SEAICECOST_JPL code

- fix few calls in SEAICECOST_JPL code where gencost_weight is passed
  as argument to S/R ECCO_READWEI & ECCO_CP

* minor adjustment for TLM

Remove "costfinal" file before running TLM in dir that might be used to run Divided-Adjoint.
This is just in case a user run a TLM testreport without cleaning the run-dir where
a Divided-Adjoint was run before (e.g., in lab_sea/run/).

* fix missing initialisation of "active_var"

- halo region of argument variable "active_var" were not initialised
  (but used later on in this S/R); fix by calling ECCO_ZERO.
- also simplify computation of "recip_nyearsRL" (now use single conversion)
  to be more robust in getting double precision results.

* document fixing minor issues in pkg/ecco

message:
Fix AB time-stepping of QuasiHydrostatic with staggerTimeStep

1) add "myTime" and "myIter" arguments to S/R MOM_QUASIHYDROSTATIC and update
  S/R calls in calc_phi_hyd.F ;
2) re-arrange mom_quasihydrostatic.F : use local array (gWinBuoy) to collects various
  (currently 2, Coriolis and NH-metric terms) contributions of quasi-hydrostatic vertical
  acceleration ; And at the end, convert vertical acceleration and add to Buoyancy argument.
  This does affect results at machine truncation level.
3) for Stagger time-step, since (Quasi) Hydrostatic pressure gradient is kept
  outside AB time-stepping (as it should for pure buoyancy contribution), needs
  to apply AB to quasi-hydro contributions (AB was previously missing here):
  Apply Adams-Bashforth extrapolation to local array gWinBuoy ; implemented
  both for AB-2 and AB-3.

author: Martin Losch <Martin.Losch@awi.de>
message:
o OBCS and PTRACERS: add open boundary support for passive tracers
  - either use homogenous (pseudo) v.Neumann conditions or prescribe
    OB-values from file; this is not different from the way theta and salinity
    are treated
  - however, Orlanski-radiation conditions are not supported, and the model
    will stop if you use pTracers and Orlanski at the same time.
  - beefed up the rountine obcs_external_fields_load: now only those open
    boundary values are overwritten with values from files for which there
    are really files, otherwise the OB-fields remain untouched. This makes
    it possible to use different OBs at different ends of the domain (as
    with EXF)
  - TODO: add support for OB?w and OB?eta, which can currently not be read
    from a file.

S/R MDS_READVEC_LOC expects 2 vectors (fldRL, fldRS) as output argument.
When used to read single number (i.e., vector of length 1), passing a simple
real "_RL" instead of a vector results in miss-match argument type for ifort compiler
with "-check all" option (-devel).
Fix problem by using local vector "tmpVal(1)" to read-in and then copy to "gencost_mskTemporal".

author: Ed Doddridge <edoddridge@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Implementing QG Leith (#96)

* Initial code dump from Scott Bachman
* Flush temp, patches, hold, and saved directories
* Flush mpif.h - should be specified by optfile
* Flush CVS headers
* Add QGLeith to mom_common and mom_fluxform/vec_inv
  Also add to diagnostics and config checks
* Limit N^2 to be >0 and use fCori instead of f0
  N^2 limiter is to prevent division by zero. fCori provides the actual f value at each location, rather than using QG theory and f0.
* Add LeithQG coefficient to GMRedi
  This requires a new common block and variable in MOM_VISC.h, and a CPP flag to include it in the GMRedi files.
* Rename VAHDLTHQG -> VAHDLTHQ
  The name was too long - 9 characters, rather than the allowed 8.
* Document new LeithQG dynamic viscosity
* Describe compile time flag to use LeithQG with GM
* Flush remianing unwanted files
* Integrate LeithQG into MLadjust verification exp
  Two new variants have been added - one with, and one without, GMRedi.
* Place GM code inside GMRedi pkg
* Update comments and add to config
* Use LeithQG in verification experiment
* units for new diagnostic
* Add equations and document new parameters
* Move GM calculation completely into pkg/gmredi
* Fix floating point exceptions
* Update verification experiment for QGLeith and GM
* Improve logic flow and hide code from adjoint
  Protect QG Leith calls with CPP option
  Remove logical input parameter `useLeithQG` and deduce from value of viscC2LeithQG
  Remove GM Redi CPP option from MOM_COMMON_OPTIONS.h
* Flush unnecessary includes from GMRedi
* Update verification inputs
* Document new parameters for QGLeith
* Shorten file and subroutine names
* Set GM_LeithQG_K to zero in multithread safe manner
* describe subroutines in files add diag arguments
  In detail:
  - add myThid, myTime, myIter to subroutine arguments
  - add description paragraph with CBOP and CEOP syntax
  - add comments describing each input and output
  - add QGL_epsil as a local variable
  - use double precision integers
* Remove special calculations for k=1 and k=Nr
  Now use klowC and ksurfC to define vertical limits, and definie vertical offsets to allow the same code to work regardless.
  Removed smoothing of Nsq.
* Average variables to correct locations on the grid
* Include QGLeith when calculating GM streamfunction
  Required adding myIter and myTime to the arguments for GMREDI_CALC_PSI_B
* Avoid division by zero
* Update testreport outputs after algorithm changes
* Flush redundant call to compute coefficient
* Shift coefficient to correct location on grid
* myTime to RL, correct order myTime, myIter, myThid
* Square array, not index. Limit division by zero
  These changes remove the floating point exception.
* Protect subroutine calls by if statement
  If QG Leith coefficient is zero, don't bother with the computation.
* Move factor inside sqrt, where it belongs
* Save sigmaRfield for QG-Leith
  sigmaRfield is used by ECCO (sometimes) and QG Leith - compute it in do_oceanic_phys.F and store   it in a common block so that it can be reused.
* Refactor code to use sigmaRfield from common block
  sigmaRfield is computed in do_oceanic_phys.F, stored in a common block, and used by QG-Leith.
  This removes the need for the costly recomputation of density in QG-Leith.
* Update output after code changes
  New code deals with surface and bottom levels more elegantly, which changed the output slightly.
* Document cpp flag for using QG Leith in GM
* Flush duplicate maskW multiplication
* few minor edits
  - remove consecutive blank lines ;
  - reduce differences vs original version
* fix length of diagUnits setting for new diagnostics
* fix computation of GM_PsiY
  - correct averaging of GM_LeithQG_K in GM_PsiY computation
  - for now, keep same argument list for this S/R (no real reason to change it)
* fix few problems and change argument list
  - fix type of "myTime" argument and fix ordering (to match calling S/R).
  - pass "GM_leithQG_K" array as argument (without bi,bj); don't need to include
   GMREDI.h anymore (Note: could be moved to pkg/mom_common).
  - allow to be compiled even without pkg/mom_common.
  - fix filling of diagnostics (+allow to compile without pkg/diagnostics).
* adjust calls after changing 2 S/R argument list
  - update after changing argument list of S/R GMREDI_CALC_QGLEITH
    and after changing back arg. list of S/R GMREDI_CALC_PSI_B
  - few edits to have terms added in same order as with K3D
* reduce difference vs original code

author: Torge Martin <torge.martin@gmail.com>
message:
Introducing a new parameterization for grease ice,
 i.e. newly formed sea ice in open water:

What it does:
 The grease ice parameterization delays formation of solid
 sea ice from frazil ice by a time constant and provides a
 dynamic calculation of the initial solid sea ice thickness
 HO as a function of winds, currents and available grease ice
 volume. Grease ice does not significantly reduce heat loss
 from the ocean in winter and area covered by grease is thus
 handled like open water.
 (for details see Smedsrud and Martin, 2014, Ann.Glac.)

How to use:
- enable SEAICE_GREASE in SEAICE_OPTIONS.h
- set SItrName(1) = 'grease' in namelist SEAICE_PARM03 in data.seaice
  then output SItr01 is SItrNameLong(1) = 'grease ice volume fraction',
  with SItrUnit(1) = '[0-1]', which needs to be multiplied by SIheff
  to yield grease ice volume.
- additionally, the actual grease ice layer thickness
  (diagnostic SIgrsLT) can be saved.

message:
New script to generate "broken-lines"

Use a different (and simpler) method to find broken-lines for Meridional Transp.
Strean-Function than the matlab-scripts in dir "bk_line".
This method is based on tagging grid-cell center according to latitude position
relative to target-latitude vector "yLat"; and then collecting the interface
edges (i.e., velocity grid-point) that separate 2 adjacent center grid-cell
with a jump in tag value across the corresponding latitude target.

Also add an example script that computes Merid. Transp. Stream-Function.

  storage arrays ; stop if trying to use QuasiHydrostatic with staggerTimeStep
  while this new option is not defined.

author: Joeran <joeran@bosma.co>
message:
Major refactoring and bugfixes for data preprocessed by nnUNet

Refactoring:
- move steps to generate a single pair to a separate function, generate_single_pair and update generate_pair.
- rename data_augmentation to random_flip_all_axes and update generate_pair.
- added documentation about expected inputs and outputs

Bugfixes for data preprocessed by nnUNet:
- change axes of random_flip_all_axes from [0, 1, 2] to [-1, -2, -3] to allow any number of preceding dimensions (e.g., multiple MRI modalities)
- change points in nonlinear_transformation to allow z-score normalisation (instead of [0, 1] range)
- apply local_pixel_shuffling to all modalities instead of the first only
- update image_in_painting  and image_out_painting to work with a single modality, allowing per-modality in & out painting

author: Jiancheng <jekyll4168@icloud.com>
message:
a bug on softamx and K.set_image_data_format("channels_first")

Hi Zhou, 

We have been trying your amazing code for days, thanks for your work!

We found a bug on your README on how to use your pretrained model for segmentation.

Your model code define a channel-first implementation
```python
K.set_image_data_format("channels_first")
```
, where inputs: `B x C x D x H x W`. Thereby, your output `final_convolution` is also `B x C x D x H x W`.

If you run.
```python
output = Activation('softmax')(final_convolution)
```
The default `softmax` is compute the normalized term on the `axis=-1`, i.e. the `W`-axis, which is usually not what people want.
